newsitem.title: USA: Jewish group protests Palestinian AIDS accusation.
newsitem.headline: Jewish group protests Palestinian AIDS accusation.

text.p: A Jewish group on Wednesday protested a Palestinian diplomat's claim before the U.N. Human Rights Commission that the Israeli army injected 300 Palestinian children with the AIDS virus.

In a letter to the president of the Geneva-based Commission on Human Rights, the World Jewish Congress asked that comments by the Palestinian observer to that group be labeled "baseless, false and intolerable in the Commission of Human Rights."

In a March 11 commission debate on human rights in the Middle East, Palestinian diplomat Nabil Ramlawi said, "the crime of genocide committed by the Israeli occupation authorities against the Palestinian people are many and varied."

He said they included "the massacre of Deir Yassin 1948, the Sabra and Shatilla massacre in Beirut in 1982, and recently when the Israeli authorities have infected by injection 300 Palestinian children with the HIV virus during the years of the Intifada."
Morris Abram, the WJC's observer at the Human Rights Commission in Geneva, said in a letter to Commission President Miraslov Somol that the remarks were "scandalous and false."
WJC Executive Director Elan Steinberg said the remarks were "a vile and destructive lie that harms the peace process which the WJC has vigorously supported."

Ramlawi said the report was confirmed by an Israeli newspaper but Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said it originated in the Egyptian newspaper al-Dostor and was picked up by al-Ahram, which later denied the report and issued an apology.

"In any event, under no circumstances has Israel ever carried out such activity and it is regrettable that the Palestinian representative at the U.N. Commission for Human Rights chose to ignore the denial and use false information," Netanyahu's office said.
